name: Ask More Photos popup — mobile number field validations
description: TC_AFP_C05. Feeds five invalid mobile numbers into the Ask More Photos login popup and asserts each one is rejected. No valid number is ever submitted, so no OTP SMS is sent and no lead is created.

placeholders.${product_url}: suite parameter — DesignTest JDMart product page under test

Open the login popup that carries the mobile number field
Confirm the popup opened before any validation is exercised

before.why: Record the Continue button's starting state — it ships disabled, and every assertion below is that an invalid entry does not enable it
Baseline: Continue is disabled on an empty field

Verified live: the field truncates 11 digits to the first 10 rather than showing an error, so 'rejected' means the 11-digit value never lands in the field. Asserting submit stays disabled here would fail — see the FINDING note.
104.note: Deliberately NOT asserting the Continue button here: truncation yields a valid 10-digit number, which legitimately enables submission.

notes: FINDING — the testcase's Expected column says a validation error 'Please enter a valid mobile number' is displayed. Probing the live DesignTest build with 98765, abcdefghij and 0000000000 produced NO new element carrying error text, and no [class*=err] or [class*=valid] node appeared anywhere. On this build the rejection is expressed only as (a) the input mask refusing non-digits and (b) the Continue button keeping its 'disbld' class. This flow asserts what the product actually does. Whether the missing inline error is a product gap or an inaccurate Expected column is a question for the author of TC_AFP_C05 — it is deliberately NOT asserted here, because asserting an element that does not exist would fail every run for the wrong reason.

FINDING (TC_AFP_C05 step 5, '11 digits') — the field carries maxlength=15 but truncates an 11-digit entry to its first 10 digits: typing 98765432101 leaves 9876543210 in the field, which is a VALID number, so Continue correctly becomes enabled. The step's stated expectation ('validation error / submit disabled') can therefore never hold through the UI. This flow asserts the truncation instead. Two things for the testcase author: (a) the 11-digit case is unreachable as written, and (b) truncation silently produces a DIFFERENT valid mobile number — if a user fat-fingers an extra digit and taps Continue, the OTP goes to a number they did not intend. This flow never clicks Continue, so no OTP was sent to the truncated number during verification.

OBSERVATION (not asserted) — the field also rewrites some 10-digit entries: 1234567890 becomes 23456789 and 0000000000 becomes 00000000. Continue stays disabled in both cases, so the testcase's intent holds and this flow asserts only that. The rewriting itself looks like input-mask behaviour worth a separate question to the product team.

Continue-button state is read via its class attribute containing 'disbld' rather than a locator on the disabled state. 'disbld' is a state class, and a locator that embeds state cannot distinguish 'button is disabled' from 'button is missing' — reading the attribute keeps the two apart.
No valid mobile number is entered anywhere in this flow, so it sends no OTP SMS and creates no lead. It is safe to re-run.
